14 A submarine has circular windows of diameter 0.30 m. The windows can experience a maximum
external pressure of 660 kPa before they crack.
What is the minimum external force needed to crack the windows?
A
47 000 N
B
190 000 N
C
310 000 N
D
620 000 N

hints: Notice the window is circular with diameter $0.30 \text{ m}$, so first find the radius $0.15 \text{ m}$ for the area.
Connect pressure to force with $p = F/A$, so the cracking force is $F = pA$ with $p = 660 \text{ kPa} = 660000 \text{ Pa}$.
Calculate the circular area $A = \pi r^2$ and then multiply by $660000 \text{ Pa}$ to get $F$ in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: diameter $d = 0.30 \text{ m}$ so radius $r = d/2 = 0.15 \text{ m}$, and maximum pressure $p = 660 \text{ kPa} = 660000 \text{ Pa}$.
State the governing relation: pressure is force per unit area, $p = F/A$, so $F = pA$.
Calculate the window area: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (0.15 \text{ m})^2 \approx 0.0707 \text{ m}^2$.
Substitute to find the force: $F = 660000 \text{ Pa} \times 0.0707 \text{ m}^2 \approx 46650 \text{ N}$.
Check units: $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{N m}^{-2} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{N}$, and round to about $47000 \text{ N}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Force equals $660000 \text{ Pa}$ times $\pi(0.15 \text{ m})^2$, giving about $47000 \text{ N}$.

B.explanation: This is too large and results from using diameter as radius or mishandling $\pi r^2$ for the $0.30 \text{ m}$ window.

C.explanation: This is too large and can come from using $0.30 \text{ m}$ as radius in $\pi r^2$ instead of $0.15 \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This is far too large and can come from using diameter in place of radius and an extra factor of 2 in area.
